<section class="content-section">
<div class="section-heading">
<div class="eyebrow">What we study</div>
<h2>Four connected research themes</h2>
<p>Our work is organized around durable scientific questions rather than individual short-term projects.</p>
</div>

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .research-card}
<div class="card-index">01</div>
### Affective Representation
How emotions and affective experiences are organized across sensory modalities, individuals, tasks, and stimulus domains.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .research-card}
<div class="card-index">02</div>
### Multivariate Methods
Developing and applying methods that treat psychological patterns, geometry, and relational structure as primary scientific objects.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .research-card}
<div class="card-index">03</div>
### Brain & Physiology
Studying affect and cognition with neuroimaging and psychophysiological measures, with emphasis on multivariate structure and generalization.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .research-card}
<div class="card-index">04</div>
### Humans & Artificial Intelligence
Comparing human and artificial representational systems and using modern AI systems in psychological research.
:::
:::
</section>
